title: Anthropic to Open Its Books to Investors as AI Lab Financials Drive the Tech Trade
excerpt: The Claude developer will present third-quarter figures to institutional investors this week, with a confidential SEC filing already in and a possible listing ahead.
body:
• Anthropic will present third-quarter financial figures to institutional investors at its San Francisco headquarters this week, according to CNBC.
  • The AI lab has filed confidentially with the SEC, but its S-1 statements are not yet public — this week's numbers are the clearest look yet at its growth and profitability.
  • One open question for investors: whether Anthropic counts revenue from cloud partners the same way peers do, a choice that can materially change its reported scale.
  • Earlier shareholder briefings put second-quarter revenue above $11.5 billion, with an annualised run rate near $65 billion by the end of July.

Anthropic is preparing to share its third-quarter financial results with a group of institutional investors this week, a step that moves the Claude developer closer to a public listing and puts hard numbers at the centre of the artificial intelligence trade. The presentation, reported by CNBC and attributed to people familiar with the matter, will take place at the company's San Francisco headquarters.

Why the numbers matter now

Anthropic has filed confidentially with the US Securities and Exchange Commission earlier this year, but it has not made its S-1 financial statements public. Until it does, private briefings like this week's are the only basis investors have for valuing a company that some expect to attempt one of the largest initial public offerings on record. Prediction markets and analyst chatter have centred on a possible November listing, though the company has not confirmed a timetable.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=c6hUND8RiDU

The disclosure also lands days after rival OpenAI disclosed a revenue run rate reported near $50 billion, a figure that reset expectations across the AI sector and sent investors recalculating what the leading labs are worth. Anthropic's answer to that number — and to questions about how fast its enterprise business is growing — will shape how the market prices both companies.

The accounting question

One detail will draw particular scrutiny: how Anthropic books revenue tied to its cloud partners. The company sells Claude through Amazon and Google cloud marketplaces as well as directly, and whether partner-channel sales are counted gross or net can swing the headline revenue figure by billions. Analysts say the treatment matters because Anthropic's largest backers — Amazon and Alphabet — are also its landlords for computing capacity, and the circular flow of money between labs and hyperscalers has become a central concern in the AI trade.

Figures shared with shareholders earlier this year, reported by the Financial Times, showed second-quarter revenue above $11.5 billion, gross margins above 80 percent before partner revenue shares and training costs, and an adjusted operating profit — a metric that excludes stock-based compensation. The same reporting put the company's committed spending on computing capacity over the coming years above $500 billion, most of it with Google, Amazon and Microsoft.

"If you continue to operate at these margins and growth rates, it will be so hard to compete."

— Joey Brookhart, analyst at SemiAnalysis, on Anthropic

What investors will watch

Beyond the revenue line, investors will look for the growth rate of Claude's enterprise subscriptions, the cost of training the next model generation, and whether the adjusted profit reported for the second quarter was repeated in the third. They will also watch how much of Anthropic's revenue depends on a small number of large customers — a concentration risk that has featured in every recent AI listing.

What this means for Indian tech readers

Anthropic is already woven into India's IT industry: HCLTech signed a partnership with the company this month to build a dedicated agentic AI business unit, and Indian engineers form a significant share of the workforce at both Anthropic and its enterprise customers. A public listing would create the first pure-play market benchmark for the model-lab business that Indian IT firms are repositioning themselves around — and its valuation will set expectations for how much of the AI value chain sits with the labs versus the services companies.

What's next

The investor presentation is expected Wednesday. If the numbers support the growth story told to shareholders earlier this year, attention will shift to the public S-1 filing, which would put audited figures — including the partner-revenue treatment — on the record for the first time.
